question: Independence Day is celebrated at the national level at _______ in Delhi.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Red Fort**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Red Fort was constructed by **Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan in 1638** as part of his new capital, Shahjahanabad (now Old Delhi).
 
• The fort is built in red sandstone and is a fine example of Mughal architecture, blending Persian, Timurid, and Indian styles.
 
• **In 2007,** the Red Fort was designated a** UNESCO World Heritage Site** for its historical and architectural significance.
 
• It served as the residence of Mughal emperors and is the site where the Prime Minister of India hoists the national flag on Independence Day (August 15) every year.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Taj Mahal**

 
 
• The Taj Mahal was commissioned by **Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan in 1632** as a mausoleum for his wife Mumtaz Mahal, **completed in 1648.**
 
• It is an outstanding example of Mughal architecture, combining elements of Persian, Indian, and** Islamic styles,** primarily built in white marble.
 
• The Taj Mahal was declared a **UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983** and is recognized as one of the **Seven Wonders of the World**.
 
• The Taj Mahal is often referred to as a symbol of eternal love, as it was built to honor Shah Jahan’s beloved wife.
 
 
 
• **India Gate**
 
 
• India Gate was designed by **Sir Edwin Lutyens and inaugurated in 1931 **as a war memorial to honor the Indian soldiers who died during **World War I and the Third Anglo-Afghan War.**
 
• The structure is **42 meters tall,** built in sandstone, and resembles the Arc de Triomphe in Paris.
 
• **In 1971, the Amar Jawan Jyoti **(Flame of the Immortal Soldier) was added under the arch to commemorate the soldiers who died in the **1971 Indo-Pak War.**
 
• India Gate is situated in New Delhi and forms a key part of the ceremonial avenue Rajpath, which hosts the Republic Day Parade every year.
 
 
 
• **Gateway of India**
 
 
• The Gateway of India was **built in 1924** to commemorate the visit of **King George V and Queen Mary to India in 1911.**
 
• It is designed in the Indo-Saracenic architectural style, combining elements of **Hindu and Muslim architecture,** and is made primarily of basalt.
 
• The Gateway of India is located in Mumbai, overlooking the Arabian Sea, and has historically served as a symbolic entrance to India for important dignitaries.
 
• The monument also marks the symbolic point where the last **British troops left India in 1948**, signifying the end of British rule after India's independence.
